About this study guide

Jet Schoolhouse is a study aid only. It is not approved training and must never be used to operate an aircraft. It is not issued, endorsed, or approved by any aircraft manufacturer, training provider, regulator, or aviation authority. Where the study guide differs from any approved or operational documentation, the approved or operational documentation always controls. Your use is covered by the Jet Schoolhouse Terms of Use and Privacy Notice.

This tool supports four ways to study: Full Quiz (a 50-question test sampled in proportion to system size, similar in spirit to a real written exam), Sequential Review (every question, in ground-school order), Study by System (drill one system's question bank directly), and Functional Checks (Fuel System and Standby Rudder, step by step). Progress and completion are tracked separately for each.

How “Proficient” is determined

Each system tile can show a “Proficient” badge once you've made sufficient attempts in that system to assess proficiency. It's a rolling calculation, recalculating fresh each time you study that system — reflecting where you stand right now, not where you stood months ago.

A few design choices behind this, briefly:

  • Why recent attempts, not a lifetime average. Rolling, recent-performance criteria are standard practice in adaptive learning systems, used at scale by platforms like ASSISTments and Khan Academy (Pelánek & Řihák, 2017).
  • Why no extra credit for a fast correct answer. A first-attempt correct answer isn't necessarily a clean read on knowledge — multiple-choice items can be answered correctly through elimination or item-writing cues rather than actual mastery, an effect the research literature calls “test-wiseness” (Smith, 1982; Downing, 2002). Every correct answer counts the same, regardless of which attempt it took.
  • Why the badge fades with inactivity. Proficiency measured once doesn't stay true forever. This mirrors the shift aviation training itself has made away from hours-based training toward proficiency-based training, under programs like the FAA's Advanced Qualification Program (AQP) and ICAO/IATA Competency-Based Training and Assessment (CBTA) — an idea that traces back to Bloom's mastery learning model (1968).

This is a study aid, not a certifying instrument. “Proficient” means your recent performance on this system meets a defined bar — it's a prompt to keep practicing where it's absent, not a substitute for instructor evaluation or an actual checkride.

Functional Checks

Fuel System Check

Starting condition

APU running, fed by the L MAIN boost pump. All other boost pumps OFF. REMOTE FUELING SHUTOFF open (switch dark). X FLOW and INTER TANK closed (switches dark), so the right side has no fuel pressure: R Fuel Pressure Low.

How this check works

  • Work the fuel panel and watch the synoptic: each boost pump in turn feeds both sides through the open crossflow valve, and the CAS shows a side with no pressure.
  • Click or tap the switch in the dashed box; the check list ticks off each step.
  • Pumps react at once. X FLOW and INTER TANK take 2 seconds: the white bar illuminates and the cyan Valve Open message displays at OPEN; the bar extinguishes and the message clears at CLOSED. A warning posts shortly after pressure is lost and clears when it returns.
  • This is a practice trainer — nothing here is scored.

On the check screen

  • Help — brings this page back without losing your place.
  • From Memory — hides the check list, instructions and dashed boxes. After three wrong tries the right control is outlined; at the end the full list shows. Click or tap again for the list.
  • Sound Off / On — off to start; click or tap to hear the chimes. It stays as you set it.
  • RESET (in the picture) begins the check again; ← Home leaves it.
Fuel System Check — work the fuel panel switches in the dashed boxes
Standby Rudder Functional Check

Starting condition

On the ground, preflight. Engines not running; STBY RUD off.

How this check works

  • Click or tap the STBY RUD switch on the synoptic to turn it ON. The AUX pump starts and supplies 3000 psi.
  • The rotary valve stays where it is, so the AUX pump pressurizes the items downstream of the valve — NWS, Main Door, Flaps / Gnd Spl Ctrl and Brakes. YD1 is not powered.
  • Click or tap it again to turn it OFF — the AUX pump stops.
  • This is a practice trainer — nothing here is scored.

On the check screen

  • Help — brings this page back without losing your place.
  • ← Home — leaves the check.
Preflight — press the STBY RUD switch to see its effect on the hydraulic system
Engine Fire Detection Fault Test

Starting condition

Aircraft powered. No fire or fault indications.

How this check works

  • In the airplane, the FAULT TEST switch is spring-loaded out. You must hold it in for the test; when you take your finger off, it springs back out and the test ends.
  • Here, one click or tap stands in for pressing and holding. Click or tap FAULT TEST on the FIRE DETECTION panel; it shows HOLDING until you click or tap it again.
  • Two chimes sound and the eight amber indications illuminate. The check list on the right ticks off each item.
  • Click or tap the switch again to let go of it. Everything extinguishes and the CAS message clears.
  • This is a practice trainer — nothing here is scored.

On the check screen

  • Help — brings this page back without losing your place.
  • Sound Off / On — off to start; click or tap to hear the chimes. It stays as you set it.
  • RESET (in the picture) begins the check again; ← Home leaves it.
Engine Fire Detection Fault Test — press and hold the FAULT TEST switch
Ground Spoiler System Check

Starting condition

On the ground, hydraulic power on. GND SPLR OFF, both power levers at IDLE.

How this check works

  • The ground spoilers can't be seen from the cockpit: confirm them on the Flight Controls synoptic (top of the screen) or with a ground observer. The ailerons work as ground spoilers: check that both move with the spoiler panels.
  • Steps 1 and 2 tick off as the check opens. Then click or tap the control in the dashed box; only the next control responds.
  • After each step, check the spoilers on the synoptic and the CAS. The red Ground Spoiler warning must never display.
  • This is a practice trainer — nothing here is scored.

Ground Spoiler System Check — work the switch and the power levers in order
Flight Controls Check

Starting condition

On the ground, hydraulic power on. Flaps 10, the Flight Controls synoptic displayed, surfaces stowed.

How this check works

  • The pilot flying does every step. The pilot monitoring needn't repeat the full check, but should make sure the yoke moves to the stops in both axes with no jams.
  • Steps 1 to 3 tick off as the check opens. The check may be done at any flap setting; spoiler deflection depends on flap position.
  • Click or tap the control in the dashed box. The yoke and the pedals may be checked in either direction first.
  • Compare the synoptic with the expected positions at the top right; a deflected surface is shaded green.
  • If the proper green fill doesn't show, make sure roll trim is fully centered.
  • This is a practice trainer — nothing here is scored.

On the check screen

  • Help — brings this page back without losing your place.
  • From Memory — hides the check list, instructions and dashed boxes. After three wrong tries the right control is outlined; at the end the full list shows. Click or tap again for the list.

Pressurization System Check

Starting condition

On the ground, AC power on. CABIN PRESSURE CONTROL in AUTO and LANDING, TROV open (on the ground it opens to depressurize the airplane). SMC on the UTILITY page. Pilot's altimeter 29.92.

How this check works

  • Check manual control of the outflow valve (TROV) on the first flight of the day.
  • With EMED closed and APU Bleed ON, moving the TROV causes pressure variations; consider APU Bleed OFF if you do the check with EMED closed.
  • Click or tap the control in the dashed box.
  • MAN HOLD is spring-loaded to center. One click or tap on DESCEND or CLIMB stands in for holding it (HOLDING); it is released for you at fully closed and again at midpoint.
  • The amber light blinks while the TROV moves and is steady when it stops fully closed.
  • This is a practice trainer — nothing here is scored.

  • RESET (in the picture) begins the check again; ← Home leaves it.

Fuel Boost Pump Check (First flight of the day)

Starting condition

First flight of the day, both engines just started and at idle. Engines started on the MAIN boost pumps: L and R MAIN ON, L and R ALT OFF. Crossflow and intertank closed. APU running, APU bleed ON, engine bleeds OFF. No CAS messages.

How this check works

  • Engine bleeds stay OFF: bleed air raises idle HP 2 to 6% and can keep the advisories from posting.
  • Click or tap the pump in the dashed box; each is its own switch, so turn a pair one after the other.
  • Turn the second MAIN pump OFF within 5 seconds of the first and you see L-R Fuel Pressure Low; wait longer, and the first side's message posts on its own first.
  • A red warning posts with three chimes. Engine Fuel Pressure (cyan) posts with one chime and clears 3 to 5 seconds after the red message; the check waits for it, in real time.
  • If L-R Engine Fuel Pressure doesn't clear, maintenance must troubleshoot before dispatch.
  • This is a practice trainer — nothing here is scored.

On the check screen

  • Help — brings this page back without losing your place.
  • From Memory — hides the check list, instructions and dashed boxes. After three wrong tries the right control is outlined; at the end the full list shows. Click or tap again for the list.
  • Sound Off / On — off to start; click or tap to hear the chimes. It stays as you set it.
  • RESET (in the picture) begins the check again; ← Home leaves it.
Fuel Boost Pump Check — click or tap the pumps in the dashed boxes
L / R Engine Fire Test

Starting condition

Aircraft powered. No fire indications.

How this check works

  • In the airplane, each FIRE TEST switch is spring-loaded out. You must hold it in for the test; when you take your finger off, it springs back out and the test ends.
  • Here, one click or tap stands in for pressing and holding. Click or tap L ENG or R ENG, in either order; it shows HOLDING until you click or tap it again.
  • Three chimes sound and every indication for that side illuminates. The check list on the right ticks off each item, in the order the book lists them.
  • Click or tap the switch again to let go of it. Everything extinguishes and the CAS messages clear. Then test the other side.
  • One switch at a time: while one is held, the other does nothing.
  • This is a practice trainer — nothing here is scored.

On the check screen

  • Help — brings this page back without losing your place.
  • Sound Off / On — off to start; click or tap to hear the chimes. It stays as you set it.
  • RESET (in the picture) begins the check again; ← Home leaves it.
L / R Engine Fire Test — press and hold each FIRE TEST switch, one at a time
